original.description: This activity will evaluate the technical and commercial feasibility of developing a standardised and interoperable set of Flat Panel User Terminal (UT) building blocks and internal interfaces, able to be reused in end user equipment designed for deployment across a broad range of market sectors and network types.The objective is to support the creation of a scalable, industrialised and costcompetitive ecosystem for flat panel user terminals in the ESA Member States by enabling economies of scale through open architectures and harmonised specifications.The activity will also identify standardised FPA terminal profiles (classes'), defining their RFperformance characteristics and associated validation and certification methodologies, to facilitate objective performance assessment and enable fair and interoperable competition among vendors.

original.description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of resilient PNT payload technologies based on digital and AI-enabled architectures. The study will investigate reconfigurable, software-defined payloads capable of characterizing and adapting to dynamic, congested or impaired RF environments.The activity will address the full signal chain, from generation to transmission, including onboard processing and AI-based techniques. A digital twin environment is also foreseen to be developed to support validation andperformance assessment.The objective is to mature concept and associated key payload technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible, flight-representative architecture for next-generation PNT systems.

original.description: The objective(s) of this activity are the following:a) Design and implement an end-to-end Space Segment testbed that can constitute a security reference architecture, including a number of cyber security building blocks.b) Perform a security assessment and verification of the implemented security measures using the selected cyber security building blocks.c) Identify potential security enhancements, that can constitute candidates for further technical developments into products.The targeted current Technology ReadinessLevel (TRL) of this activity is 4 [RD1].WORK TO BE PERFORMED1 Work LogicThe work will be organised in two phases and the following tasks:Phase 1: Definition of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 1: State-of-the-art survey of mission scenarios, security threats, relevant legislations and regulations and security technologiesoTask 2: Consolidationof Space Segment modular security reference architecture, including identification of required cyber security building blocks andspecification of system Space Segment security requirements.oTask 3: Specification of Space Segment testbed requirements (including incorporated cyber security building blocks), design and implementation and test planningPhase 2: Development, implementation and testing of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 4: Development of the Space Segment testbedoTask 5: Space Segment Testbed Testing, Security Assessment and Vulnerability MitigationoTask 6: Lessons learnt and proposed roadmap for further (other than [RD16] building blocks development (including high level specifications)Note that phase 2 will be authorised to implement the agreed building blocks, subject to a successful Phase 1 and acceptance of a proposal for the conversion of the Phase 2 price from ceilingprice to Firm Fixed Price.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 54 Mbaud DVB-S2 and 5G NR demodulator on a low-end Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) or Central Processing Unit (CPU).Targeted Improvements: Enabling a 54 Mbaud software defined radio for low end platforms not existing today in ESA Member States.Description: Previous projects have demonstrated that carriers of equivalent bandwidth can be demodulated in software on x86 server-level CPUs. Also, by using high-performance GPUs and parallel processing, bandwidths of hundreds of MHz or even many GHz could be demodulated. To date, a low-cost GPU or CPU-based demodulation solution with typical consumer terminal performance have not been developed. Such technology would allow field-upgradable terminals that can enable the deployment of new waveforms without expensive hardware swaps in the middle of the life of the system.This activity will develop and test a software-based demodulator running in a consumer GPU as found in a games console or a PC graphics card or a low-end CPU (Intel Core i3 or equivalent), with a throughput equivalent to a TV receiver or a consumer satellite broadband terminal. Superior demodulation algorithms than those in common open-source Software Defined Radio (SDR) toolkits will be studied and further developed and implemented.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall implement and test a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on one of the hardware platforms described above. The DVB-S2/X demodulator software will be tested against a hardware modulator or dedicated test equipment in the relevant environment to ensure the baud rate is met and fully compliant with as a minimum theDVB-S2 specification. Phase 1 deliverable will be a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on a low-end CPU or GPU platform. Budget is up to 700 kEuro.- Phase 2 shall implement and test in the relevant environment 5G-NR waveform or other proprietary waveform development on the hardware platform delivered by Phase 1.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: Objective: The activity objective is to design, manufacturing and test a high-performance programmable reference oscillator basedon microelectromechanical (MEMS) resonator operating in the 10 - 500 MHz range to serve as a reference oscillator or to attend directly as local oscillator the lower frequency range for telecom application.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European or Canadian source of a MEMS oscillator chip suitable for system on chip (SoC) integration.- Size, weight and power reduction by several orders of magnitude versus current technology of quartz OCXO.- Increase of fractional-N frequency generation by a factor of more than5.Description:Current telecom satellite payload equipment used mainly quartz-based oscillators for clock generation reference signals, used for track-and-hold amplifiers and digital-to-analogue (DAC) and analogue-to-digital (ADC) blocks in direct conversion (zero-IF or homodyne) frequency converters; for I-Q demodulator blocks in fully digital beamforming networks; and in double conversion super heterodyne frequency converters local oscillators (LOs) at different carrier frequencies. However, European sources of quartz-based oscillatorsare becoming more limited, and these solutions are expensive, with a form factor and power consumption that becomes challenging when incorporating into highly integrated payloads. Current state-of-art oscillators based on microelectromechanical(MEMS) resonators display competitive phase noise and frequency stability performance compared to quartz-based solutions, but thereare no European or Canadian sources of such products. Important advantages of such MEMS resonators compared to quartz-based oscillatorcan be seen, where MEMS achieves performance in between the Temperature Controlled Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) and Oven ControlledCrystal Oscillators (OCXOs) but with the advantage of their extremely small form factor, low power consumption and integration capability with Silicon process. One more important aspect is that the MEMS fundamentalmode frequency can be much higher than that of aQuartz crystal, whereas cost reduction is expected at lower frequencies and better performance at higher frequencies.This activity will design, manufacture of an engineering model oscillator chip based on European microelectromechanical technology in the 10 and500 MHz frequency range. The performance shall be suitable for a range of application scenarios in telecom payloads. The engineering model chip shall be built and tested in a critical environment, including thermal test

original.description: Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. The technology to be developed is to model accurately the complex physical processes at the gas surface interface during ascent and descent, in which different coatings are experimental tested validating the predictive capabilitiesof the numerical models. The model will include advanced kinetics, using a hybrid state-to-state -Multi-Temperature (StS-MT) derived from the StS, where the vibrational degrees of freedom are described by the vibrational temperature, while electronic excited states are treated as independent species, in order to estimate the radiative properties. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development of a chemical model of air interacting with the Si-O-C ceramic material, in dissociation regime; - Development of a hybrid StS-MT kinetic model - Develop a database for thermodynamic properties and of transport cross sections for air including Si-O-C species - Implementation of kinetics and transport in a numerical tool for hypersonic flows for the reliable simulation, flat plate/coupons - Model chemical gas surface interaction, chemical stability, roughness, thickness, stability of coatings, catalyst by experimental plasma testing of different samples, thermal optical properties, emission spectroscopy - Numerical modelling and testing thermal bounding of the silica based substrate bounding with the coating, testing of the attachment devices - Evaluation of differentceramics suitable for the orbital entry conditions.
